main.job: existence and having: there is / I have
main.why: Turkish has no 'have' verb; var carries both existence and possession.

main.job: non-existence and not having: there isn't / I don't have
main.why: Other half of the var/yok pair; hugely frequent in shops and daily talk.

main.job: negating identity or description: is not / am not
main.why: Negation for nouns and adjectives; English speakers wrongly reach for verb negation or yok.

main.job: turning a statement into a yes/no question
main.why: The only way to ask yes/no questions; vowel harmony and placement trip learners.
Want + verb is a core building block.

main.job: can / be able to do something
main.why: Ability and permission are built with this suffix, not a separate verb.
The everyday spoken way to say 'I have to' and 'I need'.

main.job: I mean / so (rephrasing and concluding in talk)
main.why: One of the most frequent spoken fillers; learners hear it constantly.
The compact way to give an opinion; needed to join conversation.
Very frequent postposition for comparing and describing.

jobs_covered.identity: zero copula in 3rd person; negated with değil
jobs_covered.people: person is marked on verb endings; pronoun set (6) not started at count 10

shape.notes: Bare A2–B1 list, building blocks first, then glue. Pronoun set and personal 'be' endings left out as A1 sets too large for 10 slots. No greetings or nouns.
